title: ESC-29: the extraction prompt excludes CPUs and chipsets but not graphics cards
body:
One row appended to `docs/escapes.md`. The ledger is append-only and nothing above it is touched.

`prompts/extract-claims.md` tells the model to skip claims about a CPU, a chipset in general, or the industry. **It never mentions graphics cards.** Buildzoid reviews those too, and those videos reach the corpus because the alias list finds real motherboard names inside them — which is correct and wanted, since he discusses the board he is testing on. The model then does exactly what it was told and records every claim about a named product, so a GPU PCB breakdown yields dozens of well-formed, correctly-categorised, verbatim-quoted claims about a product this project is not about.

Measured on the first full extraction: **2771 claims across 91 bundles, 35 of them unambiguously about graphics cards** and roughly 90 more from GPU-topic videos. Every one passed the schema, because `claims.py` validates SHAPE and a claim about an RTX 4090 satisfies every field rule perfectly.

**The gap: the prompt is a committed artifact that no gate reads.** `prompt_text()` guards its existence — a missing prompt is a named failure — and nothing guards its content. No check asserts that what the prompt excludes matches what the project is about. The blind-authorship split does not help either: both agents are handed the same spec, and the spec did not mention graphics cards. It surfaced because a person read a sample of the output and recognised a graphics card, which is what makes it an escape rather than a caught defect.

**The row is candid that the test landing with the fix is the weaker half.** It pins a phrase, and the next omission will be a product that phrase does not name. Two better candidates are recorded: a check over the claim STORE rather than the prompt, which fires on the next omission whatever its wording; and rewriting the exclusion as a rule about non-motherboard components rather than an enumeration of the ones someone thought of.

**This lands first, on its own**, per the ordering ESC-20 records — the ledger entry, then the plan citing it, then the work. The previous attempt (#210) bundled the fix with an unplanned document and was blocked for exactly that, correctly.

Ran locally: `escapes-append-only.sh` — 13 landed rows intact.
